title: API 510 Training in Corpus Christi: Pressure Vessel Exam Prep
description: Self-paced online API 510 exam prep with instructor Q&A for Corpus Christi inspectors working on refinery, LNG and petrochemical pressure vessels.
h1: API 510 Training in Corpus Christi, TX: Pressure Vessel Inspector Exam Prep for Ship Channel Refineries and San Patricio County Plants
html:
API 510 training for Corpus Christi pressure vessel inspectors

Corpus Christi is a pressure-vessel town. Crude and vacuum towers, desalters, overhead accumulators, hydrotreater reactors, amine contactors, sour water strippers and shell-and-tube exchangers line the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, and across the bay in San Patricio County an LNG export terminal and an ethane cracker add separators, dryers, quench towers and caustic towers. Each needs an inspection plan, an interval and a thickness history, and owner-users on the Coastal Bend look for the API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector certification in the people who make those calls.

This page is for inspectors, NDT technicians, welders, operators and engineers in and around Corpus Christi who are preparing for the API 510 examination. The Atlantis NDT course is self-paced and online: you begin when you enrol, move at your own pace and send questions to an instructor whenever a Section VIII paragraph will not give up its meaning. There is no Atlantis classroom in Corpus Christi. The American Petroleum Institute decides who is eligible, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification, and every candidate applies to API individually. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and finishing the course does not make anyone certified.

Where API 510 work sits around Corpus Christi Bay

The U.S. Energy Information Administration's refinery capacity report, with data as of January 2026, is the public list of who runs what on the ship channel. The table draws on its Corpus Christi entries and adds Valero's inland Three Rivers refinery and the two large San Patricio County plants.

SiteOwner or operatorVessels on an inspector's list
Bill Greehey Refinery (East and West plants), on the Corpus Christi Ship ChannelValero (EIA: Valero Refining Co Texas LP, 290,000 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation)Crude and vacuum towers, coker and hydroprocessing vessels, amine and sour water systems, exchanger banks; Valero lists petroleum coke, asphalt and petrochemicals among the products
Corpus Christi West and Corpus Christi East refineriesFlint Hills Resources, a Koch company (EIA: 290,000 and 87,500 barrels per calendar day)Distillation columns, reactors and separators, drums and exchangers across two plants with different ages and layouts
Condensate and light crude distillation plantsBuckeye Texas Processing (60,000) and Magellan Processing, now part of ONEOK (50,000); EIA lists no vacuum or coking capacity at eitherFractionation columns, overhead drums, exchangers and product separators
Corpus Christi Liquefaction, San Patricio CountyCheniere; EIA reports Stage 3 finished in August 2026, making it the second-largest US LNG facilityAcid gas removal and dehydration vessels, separators and exchangers ahead of the cold section
Gulf Coast Growth Ventures, San Patricio CountyExxonMobil and SABIC in a 50/50 venture, operated by ExxonMobil; 1.8 million metric tons a year of ethane crackingQuench and caustic towers, compressor suction drums, polyethylene and glycol unit vessels
Three Rivers refinery, Live Oak CountyValero (EIA lists it under Diamond Shamrock Refining, 89,000 barrels per calendar day)A smaller inland refinery that draws on the same pool of Coastal Bend inspectors

The refineries are decades old: Valero's 2020 fact sheet says it commissioned the West plant in 1983 and acquired the East plant in 2001, and older vessels bring the repair, alteration and rerating questions that fill much of the API 510 code. The San Patricio County plants are young, so their programmes are still building thickness histories from baseline readings. An inspector comfortable with both, a long record to interpret and a short one to start, is useful on either side of the bay.

Owner-user inspection departments and the contractors around them

API 510 is written around the owner-user's inspection organisation. On the Coastal Bend that usually means a site inspection group that holds the vessel files, sets inspection plans and approves repairs, supported by inspection and NDT contractors who supply people for routine surveys and, above all, for turnarounds. Valero's 2020 fact sheet counted more than 760 employees at its Corpus Christi complex, and Flint Hills said in late 2024 that it employs more than 1,000 people full-time in Texas plus hundreds of contractors, so the contract side of the market is large as well as the in-house one.

The distinction matters for eligibility. API counts experience gained while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency, and API 510's definition of that term includes an owner-user's own inspection organisation and independent organisations working under contract to it. A contract UT technician on a refinery turnaround and a site inspector on the owner's payroll can both be building qualifying experience, provided the work is the supervision or performance of vessel inspection that API recognises. The guides to owner-user inspection organisations and in-house versus third-party inspection explain how those roles divide.

Day to day, Coastal Bend API 510 inspectors decide whether a thinned shell or nozzle can run to the next window, whether work is a repair or an alteration, what test follows welding and whether to rerate rather than replace. See the guides to repairs, alterations and rerating and pressure testing after repair; the exam asks the same questions in its open-book half.

Damage mechanisms that shape vessel inspection on the Coastal Bend

API RP 571 is part of the API 510 Body of Knowledge, although the exam draws only on the RP 571 sections that the Body of Knowledge lists. These are the mechanisms a Corpus Christi inspector is most likely to meet.

Crude unit overheads

Salts in crude hydrolyse to hydrogen chloride, which condenses with the first water in the overhead system. Overhead drums, exchanger shells and channels downstream of that dew point corrode quickly when desalting, wash water or neutraliser practice slips. RP 571 describes both the hydrochloric acid and the ammonium chloride mechanisms, but only hydrochloric acid corrosion is among the RP 571 sections listed for the API 510 exam.

Wet H2S service

Sour water strippers, amine contactors, flash drums and overhead receivers can suffer hydrogen blistering, hydrogen-induced cracking, stress-oriented hydrogen-induced cracking and sulfide stress cracking. The inspection answer is usually wet fluorescent magnetic particle examination of welds, backed by ultrasonic sizing; see crack detection in sour service.

Amine and caustic cracking

Carbon steel vessels in amine service that were never stress relieved can crack at welds, and caustic towers of the kind found at an ethane cracker carry a similar risk that depends on concentration and temperature. The guide to amine and caustic cracking sets out the inspection approach.

Cold service and brittle fracture

LNG and cracker cold sections bring minimum design metal temperature and impact testing into everyday conversations. The exam tests the same ideas through Section VIII's impact test exemption rules, so a candidate from the San Patricio County plants often finds those questions familiar.

Salt air and corrosion under insulation

Onshore winds carry salt across pipe racks and vessel skirts, and wet insulation on warm carbon steel columns is a constant concern on the bay. API 510 asks the inspection plan to consider corrosion under insulation where the vessel is susceptible, and RP 571 explains why the operating temperature decides how hard to look.

A Coastal Bend example: an overhead drum with little life left

Exam calculations test whether you pick the right rule more than your arithmetic. Here is one built on a vessel crude unit inspectors read every turnaround.

The water boot on an overhead accumulator was 0.400 in. thick when it was installed 16 years ago. Four years ago the minimum reading was 0.375 in.; today it is 0.335 in. The required thickness for the boot is 0.300 in.

  • Long-term rate: (0.400 − 0.335) ÷ 16 = 0.0041 in. per year.
  • Short-term rate: (0.375 − 0.335) ÷ 4 = 0.0100 in. per year, more than twice the long-term rate, which tells you something in the process has changed.
  • Remaining life at the short-term rate: (0.335 − 0.300) ÷ 0.0100 = 3.5 years.
  • Interval: normally the lesser of half the remaining life and 10 years. Because the remaining life is under four years, API 510 allows the interval to be the full remaining life up to a maximum of two years, so the answer is 2 years.

Two distractors are built into that question. Use the long-term rate and the remaining life comes out near 8.5 years, with an interval of about 4.3 years, which ignores the change the readings are signalling. Forget the under-four-years rule and you answer 1.75 years. API 510 leaves the choice of rate to the inspector, with a corrosion specialist; when the question gives no reason to trust the older rate, take the conservative one. The corrosion rate guide works more cases.

Fitting API 510 study around Corpus Christi turnarounds

Most local candidates already work rotating twelve-hour shifts or follow turnarounds between the ship channel, the north shore and plants up the coast, which is why a self-paced course fits. A workable approach:

  1. Pick the API exam window first, then mark the months when you expect to be on a turnaround. Put the heavy reading of Section VIII and API 510 into the gaps between them.
  2. During a turnaround, study lightly but use the job: read the nameplate and data report of each vessel you enter, and later find the matching Section VIII paragraphs for its joint efficiency, material and test pressure.
  3. Send the instructor the questions the job raises. When a site practice differs from the code text, ask which paragraph governs, because the exam scores the code.
  4. Keep the timed practice papers for the final stretch, and sit one full rehearsal on a day off.

Allow for weather as well. Hurricane season runs from June through November, and a storm on the Coastal Bend can call inspectors back to site or delay travel to a test appointment. The API exam windows and application deadlines page will help you choose a window with room around it.

Eligibility routes for Corpus Christi candidates

API's scale pairs education with years of experience, gained within the last ten years, in the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of pressure vessels, including time supervising or performing inspection. The full table is on the API 510 certification requirements page; this is how it tends to apply to people already working locally.

  • Del Mar College graduates. Del Mar's Nondestructive Testing Technology program at the Windward Campus offers an Associate of Applied Science and a Level II certificate, and its Process Technology program trains process operators for the refinery and petrochemical industries. Whether a particular credential counts as a two-year degree or certificate in engineering or technology is API's decision when it reviews your application; if it does, the requirement is two years, one of them in inspection.
  • Engineers. A graduate with a bachelor's degree in engineering, for example in chemical or mechanical engineering from Texas A&M University–Kingsville, needs one year supervising or performing vessel inspection.
  • NDT technicians. Thickness surveys, weld examinations and crack detection on vessels are the commonest local starting point; the ASNT side of that career is described on NDT training in Corpus Christi.
  • Welders and operators. Repair welding and unit operation count toward the longer routes, but API still wants one year of inspection work within the total.

Sitting the API 510 exam from the Coastal Bend

Once API accepts your application you book a seat with Prometric, which lists test centres in and around Corpus Christi; choose one when you schedule. The day is long, with a closed-book morning and an open-book afternoon in which the code PDFs are on the computer and nothing else may come into the room. Practise reading Section VIII on a screen, because finding UG-27, UG-99 or a UCS paragraph quickly in a PDF is a different skill from flipping to a tab in a paper book.

Comparing API 510 preparation options in Corpus Christi

  • Mentoring inside an owner-user inspection group. Invaluable for field judgement and experience records, though it seldom covers the whole Body of Knowledge.
  • Classroom courses run by other providers. Usually held in larger cities on fixed dates, which means travel; some candidates like the structure.
  • Self-study from the code books. Possible for disciplined readers, but open-book technique and calculation traps are easy to miss.
  • Self-paced online preparation with instructor Q&A. The Atlantis approach: the full Body of Knowledge, worked examples and timed papers, studied around your own roster.

Sponsoring API 510 candidates from a Corpus Christi site

Refineries and contractors on the Coastal Bend often prepare several people at once, ahead of a heavy turnaround year or to add certified inspectors to a rotation. One enquiry can cover a mixed group, such as two API 510 candidates and an API 570 candidate. Fees are quoted on request. Each person still applies to API in their own name, works through the material at their own pace and asks their own questions. Employers help most by signing accurate experience records and keeping exam weeks clear of call-outs. Owners who need NDE on vessels rather than training can see pressure vessel inspection services in Corpus Christi.

faq.q: Is there an in-person API 510 class in Corpus Christi?
faq.a: Not from Atlantis. The API 510 course is studied online at your own pace, with an instructor answering questions as you go, so a shift worker on the north shore and a contractor living in Portland or Robstown follow exactly the same material. Other providers sometimes run fixed-date classroom courses in larger Texas cities. Whichever way you prepare, the examination itself is taken at a Prometric test centre after API approves your application.

faq.q: Does a Del Mar College NDT degree shorten the API 510 experience requirement?
faq.a: It may. API asks for two years of pressure vessel experience, one of them in inspection, from candidates with a two-year degree or certificate in engineering or technology, instead of three years with a high school diploma. Whether Del Mar's Nondestructive Testing Technology associate degree or certificate is accepted on that line is decided by API when it reviews your application, so describe the credential accurately. See the API 510 certification page for the full scale.

faq.q: Can experience at the LNG terminal or the ethane cracker count toward API 510?
faq.a: Experience counts when it is the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of pressure vessels that API recognises, and the inspection portion is gained with an authorized inspection agency. Vessel inspection at a liquefaction plant or a cracker can qualify in the same way as refinery work. Construction experience on a new train can count on the longer routes, but API still requires a year of inspection and verifies what you declare.

faq.q: Does contract turnaround work in Corpus Christi count as API 510 experience?
faq.a: It can. API 510 recognises independent organisations working under contract to an owner-user as part of the authorized inspection agency definition, so a contractor's vessel inspector or NDT technician on a refinery turnaround may be gaining qualifying experience. Keep your own log of vessels, dates and tasks, because short contracts are easy to forget by the time you apply.

faq.q: Is the API 510 exam open book?
faq.a: Partly. Of the 170 questions, 110 are closed-book and 60 are open-book, and only the open-book part gives you the code PDFs on the computer. The closed-book morning rewards knowing API 510 and the recommended practices well enough to answer without looking, while the afternoon rewards fast navigation of Section VIII. Corpus Christi candidates used to paper code books on site should practise in PDF form well before the exam.

faq.q: Which code books do I need to study for API 510?
faq.a: The editions you need are the ones on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for your exam window, which lists API 510, the recommended practices and the ASME sections examined. You will want access to those editions while you study, either through your employer's library or your own copies bought from API and ASME. The course follows the sheet for your window and tells you which parts of each document the Body of Knowledge actually covers.

faq.q: Can a Corpus Christi refinery or contractor enrol several API 510 candidates?
faq.a: Yes. Employers often sponsor a group, and a single enquiry can include people preparing for different API examinations. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate keeps an individual login, sets their own pace and sends their own questions to the instructor, and each one applies to API separately. Tell us the number of candidates and the exam windows you are aiming for when you enquire.
